scripts.radio:
Good evening listeners, welcome to Kenya on Record, your civic accountability space.

Today, we look at the numbers hitting your pocket directly. Official reports reveal that state debt rose by a massive 233 billion shillings in just four months. 

When we hear billions, it often sounds like abstract government talk. But let us break down what this means for you and me. When public debt balloons at this speed, the government faces heavy pressure to service those loans. Where does that money come from? It comes from your pocket—through higher taxes on basic goods, increased levies on fuel, and aggressive revenue drives. At the same time, we see budget cuts in critical sectors like public health, agriculture, and public school funding.

You end up paying more at the shop, but receiving less in return. Accountability requires us to ask hard questions: What was this money borrowed for? Which projects received these funds? And are citizens getting real value?

Kwa ufupi: Deni la serikali limeongezeka kwa shilingi bilioni mia mbili thelathini na tatu kwa miezi minne pekee. Hii inamaanisha shinikizo zaidi la ushuru kwa Mkenya wa kawaida ili kulipa mikopo hiyo. Ni lazima tuhoji matumizi ya mikopo hii na kudai uwazi kikamilifu.

Keep asking the hard questions, stay informed, and let us safeguard our resources. Until next time.
scripts.voice_note:
Hujambo. Here is your quick accountability update from Kenya on Record.

In just four months, our national debt expanded by 233 billion shillings. That is not just a figure on a balance sheet—it translates directly to higher taxes, new levies, and a tighter squeeze on your household budget.

When state borrowing surges without matching public value, the burden lands squarely on citizens through increased cost of living and reduced spending on vital services like public healthcare.

We must keep tracking where every borrowed shilling goes and demand a full audit of public debt. Share this audio with your network to keep the conversation active. Stay sharp, and stay informed.
